title: Launch your first AI agent
subtitle: anthropics/launch-your-agent, Anthropic's own Claude Code skill, Apache-2.0, 940 stars

blocks.text: This is the repo from the reel. It interviews you about what you want built, scopes a v0, launches it in your own Anthropic account, grades it against your definition of done, and if the job recurs, puts it on a schedule. You do not write the agent code.
Two things to know before you start

parts: The video says "without ever touching the terminal", but the repo's own Quickstart is three terminal commands. What you actually skip is writing the agent code and wiring up APIs, which is the hard part. If three commands is a dealbreaker, stop here.

It runs on an Anthropic API key from your own account, and runs cost cents, not free credits. Put a few dollars on the account first, or the launch fails at the last step with "your credit balance is too low".

blocks.text: 1. Have Claude Code installed and signed in.
2. Clone it and open Claude Code inside the folder:
The skills in .claude/skills/ are picked up automatically because you opened Claude Code inside this folder. There is nothing to install and no marketplace to add.

parts: in your Anthropic Console: the agent, its environment, a graded run, and a scheduled deployment if your task recurs.
the build sheet, the exact API payloads it sent, a resumable launch script, an eval scaffold, an overview page, and a NEXT-DIRECTIONS.md laying out what v1 and v2 should be.

blocks.text: It is a reference implementation. Anthropic states it is not maintained and not accepting contributions: treat it as a teaching repo you fork, not a dependency you track.
It is deliberately token-heavy. It explains each step as it goes, so it burns more tokens than a purpose-built agent would. That is the trade for understanding what it built.
